# SACRAMENTO RIVER BASIN

# Pit River below Pit No. 4 Dam, Calif.

Location -Lat 40°59' long 121°47' in SW sec. 17, T. 36 N., R. 2 E., on right bank I mile downstream from Pit No. 4 Dam and 3 miles downstream from Screwdriver Creek and Pit No. 3 powerhouse.

Drainage area.--4,860 sq mi, approximately, excluding Goose Lake basin.

Records available.--July 1927 to September 1957.

Gage. Water-stage recorder. Altitude of gage is 2,345 ft (from river-profile map).

Average discharge -46 years (1911-57), , 2,665 cfs (1,929,000 acre-ft per year) including diversion to Pit No. 4 powerhouse. Period 1911-27 extrapolated on basis of records for Pit River at Big Bend.

# Pit River below Pit No. 4 Dam, Calif. (cont.)

Extremes Maximum discharge during year, 7,570 cfs Feb. 26 (gage height, 10.81 ft); min- imum daily, 58 cfs Mar. 26, 27. 1927-57: Maximum discharge, 30,200 cfs Dec. 12, 1937 (gage height, 17.90 ft), from rating curve extended above 8,000 cfs on basis of velocity-area studies; minimum daily, 54 cfs Oct. 27, 1955,

Remarks --Records good except those for periods of no gage-height record, which are fair. Flow regulated by many small reservoirs and powerplants (total usable reservoir capacity, about 200,000 acre-ft) Many diversions above station; diversion to Pit No. 4 powerhouse began June 9, 1955 (see adjustment figures, not previously published, in table below for period June 1955 to September 1956.

Cooperation.--Water-stage-recorder graph and three discharge measurements furnished by Pacific Gas & Electric Co., in connection with a Federal Power Commission project.

Revisions (water years) . -WSP 843: 1935(M). .

Diversion to Pit No. 4 powerhouse, June 1955 to September 1956
